question: What happens during Active Range of Motion (AROM) exercises?

options.A: The movement is done only while the patient is completely asleep.
options.B: A mechanical machine forces the joints to bend and straighten.
options.C: The patient moves the joints independently using their own muscle power.
options.D: The nurse or therapist moves the client's joints through space.

explanation: You've got this! AROM simply means the patient does the moving all by themselves, using their own muscles without any external push. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T2#GNS221_U1_T2_h1)

question: Why are AROM exercises great for keeping a patient's nervous system working well?

options.A: They require the brain to send nerve impulses that actively contract the muscles.
options.B: They completely eliminate the need for any other physical therapy.
options.C: They stop the patient from ever feeling tired during the hospital stay.
options.D: They force the joints to move past their normal anatomical limits safely.

explanation: Spot on! When the patient initiates the move themselves, the communication highway between the brain and muscles stays open and strong. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T2#GNS221_U1_T2_h1)

question: How do active muscle movements during AROM help with blood circulation?

options.A: They make the arteries much wider and longer permanently.
options.B: They remove all red blood cells from the lower extremities.
options.C: They act as a physical pump pushing blood back toward the heart.
options.D: They completely stop the heart from beating too fast.

explanation: Think of the muscles as a natural pump! As they squeeze, they push blood back up toward the heart against gravity, keeping clots away. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T2#GNS221_U1_T2_h2)

question: What is a major benefit of keeping synovial fluid moving inside a joint?

options.A: It cools down the body when a fever is present.
options.B: It dissolves small blood clots in the bloodstream.
options.C: It permanently locks the joint in a straight position.
options.D: It nourishes the cartilage inside the joint capsule.

explanation: Cartilage doesn't have its own blood supply, so it depends entirely on movement to swish that nourishing synovial fluid around! [learn more](GNS221_U1_T2#GNS221_U1_T2_h2)

question: When should a nurse hold off on starting AROM exercises?

options.A: Mild fatigue from staying in bed
options.C: A history of chronic mild backaches
options.D: Stable and well-controlled high blood pressure

explanation: Safety first! Moving a broken, unstable bone before it heals can displace it and cause serious harm. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T2#GNS221_U1_T2_h3)

question: Your patient just had shoulder surgery and is on bed rest. What is your next best move regarding AROM?

options.A: Encourage the patient to swing the arm rapidly to build strength quickly.
options.B: Check the medical orders and surgeon guidelines before allowing shoulder movement.
options.C: Ignore the surgery and start full arm rotations immediately.
options.D: Refuse to let the patient move any part of their entire body.

explanation: Always check the surgeon's rules first after an operation to make sure you protect the healing surgical site. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T2#GNS221_U1_T2_h3)

question: What is the very first thing a nurse should check before starting AROM with a patient?

options.A: Force the patient's joints to bend rapidly.
options.B: Administer a strong sleeping pill to the client.
options.C: Turn off all the lights in the patient room.
options.D: Check the medical record for specific joint restrictions.

explanation: Taking a quick look at the chart first ensures you don't accidentally work on a restricted or healing limb. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T2#GNS221_U1_T2_h4)

question: Why is it important to talk through the exercise steps with your patient beforehand?

options.A: It forces the muscles to relax without any effort.
options.B: It reduces anxiety and encourages the patient to cooperate safely.
options.C: It replaces the need to check vital signs or pain levels.
options.D: It completely eliminates all physical pain from arthritis.

explanation: Communication is key! When patients know what to expect, they feel less anxious and can help you keep them safe. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T2#GNS221_U1_T2_h4)

question: Generally, how many times should a specific joint movement be repeated during an AROM session?
explanation: Keep it gentle! Repeating a motion just a few times helps the patient gain benefits without wearing them out. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T2#GNS221_U1_T2_h5)

question: When you support the joint above and below the moving area during exercise, what are you doing?

options.A: To stop blood flow completely to the lower arm.
options.B: To force the joint to bend past its normal breaking point.
options.C: To replace the patient's muscle power with nurse strength.
options.D: To provide stability and protect the limb during movement.

explanation: Supporting the limbs properly keeps the movement steady and shields the surrounding tissues from unnecessary strain. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T2#GNS221_U1_T2_h5)

question: What should you do right away if a patient complains of sharp pain during AROM?

options.A: Stop the exercise right away and let the patient rest.
options.B: Scold the patient for not being strong enough.
options.C: Push harder to break through the painful barrier.
options.D: Ignore the complaint and finish the scheduled routine.

explanation: Sharp pain is a warning sign! Stop immediately and give the patient a breather to prevent injury. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T2#GNS221_U1_T2_h6)

question: Which of these tells you that a patient is getting too tired during active exercises?

options.A: Falling into a deep, heavy sleep instantly
options.C: Skin turning bright pink and warm
options.D: A sudden increase in smiling and laughing

explanation: Watch out for breathlessness or lightheadedness—these are classic signs that the patient has had enough for now. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T2#GNS221_U1_T2_h6)

question: Which of these details must you include when charting AROM exercises?

options.A: The personal phone number of the patient's family
options.B: The brand name of the bed sheets used in the room
options.C: The specific joints exercised and the number of repetitions
options.D: The exact cost of the physical therapy equipment

explanation: Good documentation means noting down exactly which joints you worked on and how many times they moved. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T2#GNS221_U1_T2_h7)

question: Why is recording how well the patient tolerated the exercise so important for the care team?

options.A: It serves as a legal punishment if the patient is lazy.
options.B: It determines the exact hospital discharge date immediately.
options.C: It stops nurses from having to write shift reports.
options.D: It helps guide future exercise plans and shows recovery progress.

explanation: Tracking progress helps the whole healthcare team decide whether to keep the routine the same or step it up next time! [learn more](GNS221_U1_T2#GNS221_U1_T2_h7)
